overview:
This is one of the most spectacular day trips in Morocco. In a single day you cross the High Atlas on one of the most scenic roads in Africa, visit the most famous ksar in the country, and see the edge of the Saharan south – red earth, palm groves and kasbahs.

The Tizi n'Tichka pass climbs to about 2,260 metres past Berber villages and walnut terraces. On the other side the landscape turns dry and red, and Ait Ben Haddou appears: a ksar of earthen houses and towers stacked on a hill above the Ounila river, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987 and the setting of films and series from Lawrence of Arabia to Gladiator and Game of Thrones. With a local guide you cross the river and climb through its lanes to the old granary at the top. After lunch you choose your second visit: Ouarzazate, with the Taourirt kasbah and the film studios, or the Glaoui kasbah of Telouet, with its painted reception rooms high in the mountains.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 12 hours
• Start and finish: your hotel or riad in Marrakech
• Distance: about 190 km each way, about 4 hours' driving each way with stops (around 400 km in total)
• Type: private day trip with your own driver; local guide at Ait Ben Haddou
• Walking: about 1.5 hours, with a steep climb inside the ksar
• Activity level: easy (long day in the car)
• Best months: all year; spring and autumn are the most comfortable

OUARZAZATE OR TELOUET?
• Ouarzazate (the classic choice): the Taourirt kasbah, a maze of earthen rooms once owned by the Glaoui family, and the film studios where sets from desert films still stand. Best for film fans and families.
• Telouet (the quieter choice): a detour on the old caravan road before Ait Ben Haddou, to the half-ruined palace of the Glaoui pashas, whose zellige tiles and painted cedar ceilings are among the finest in southern Morocco. Best for history and architecture lovers.
Tell us your choice when booking, or decide with your driver on the day.

WHY THIS TRIP WORKS
It shows you the road and landscapes of the desert tours in a single day, without a night away from Marrakech. Because it is private, your driver stops wherever you want for photos, tea or a stretch, and you set the pace at each site.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Travellers short on time, film fans, photographers, families with children who are fine with a long drive, and anyone curious to see the south before choosing a desert tour.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
The drive is long for one day. If you can spare a night, the [2-day Zagora desert tour](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/2-day-desert-tour-from-marrakech-to-zagora/685bd1a47aecbeecb2a4a7d9) adds a camel ride and a desert camp. To see the great dunes of the Sahara, take the [3-day Marrakech to Merzouga tour](/en-US/morocco/marrakech/tours/3-days-trip-from-marrakech-to-merzouga-desert/680bc6a5aa6f43072c7700f6).

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
If you suffer from car sickness, take medication before the pass and sit in front. Bring a warm layer for the pass (it is often 10 °C cooler than Marrakech), a hat and sun cream for Ait Ben Haddou, shoes with a good grip, and cash in dirhams for lunch and entrance fees.
descriptions:
What to expect: a full day on one of the most beautiful roads in Africa, a guided climb through a UNESCO-listed ksar, and a second visit of your choice in Ouarzazate or Telouet.

Your driver collects you early from your riad or hotel and heads south across the Haouz plain towards the High Atlas. The road climbs through walnut trees and red Berber villages; a good coffee stop is Taddert, where you can also visit a women's argan cooperative. Higher up, the Tizi n'Tichka pass (about 2,260 m) is the highest paved pass in Morocco, with wide views over the peaks and, in winter, snow on the summits.

AIT BEN HADDOU (about 1.5 hours)
On the southern side the land turns dry and red. At Ait Ben Haddou your local guide leads you across the Ounila river and up through the ksar: a fortified village of earthen houses, towers and alleys built on the caravan route between the Sahara and Marrakech. A few families still live inside. Your guide explains how the houses are built from rammed earth and straw, why the towers are decorated, and which films were shot here. The climb to the old granary at the top takes about 20 minutes on steep, uneven steps and rewards you with the best view over the valley and the new village on the other bank.

OUARZAZATE OR TELOUET
After lunch you visit Ouarzazate, 30 minutes further south: the Taourirt kasbah with its courtyards and painted ceilings, or one of the film studios, where you walk among sets used in desert epics. If you chose Telouet instead, the route takes the old mountain road through the Ounila valley in the morning, with its green oases and earthen villages, to the palace of the Glaoui pashas, before continuing down to Ait Ben Haddou. You then cross the Tichka again and return to Marrakech in the evening.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
07:00 – Pick-up at your hotel or riad.
08:30 – Coffee stop near Taddert (about 20 min).
09:30 – Tizi n'Tichka pass (photo stop, about 15 min).
10:30 – Telouet option: detour to the Glaoui kasbah (about 1 hour) through the Ounila valley.
11:15 – Ait Ben Haddou: guided visit (about 1.5 hours).
13:00 – Lunch near Ait Ben Haddou (about 1 hour, not included).
14:30 – Ouarzazate: Taourirt kasbah or film studios (about 1 hour).
15:45 – Departure for Marrakech.
19:30 – Drop-off in Marrakech.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Ait Ben Haddou is free to enter; some houses ask a small fee to visit inside. Entrance fees in Ouarzazate and Telouet are paid on the spot.
• The road has many bends; it is fully paved and safe, and drivers do it every week.
• Wear shoes with a good grip for the steps of the ksar.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, pick-up and drop-off in Marrakech, local guide at Ait Ben Haddou, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, entrance fees, drinks, tips.

IF THE WEATHER TURNS: in winter the pass can be closed by snow for a few hours. Your driver checks the road reports before leaving and adapts the timing. After heavy rain the river at Ait Ben Haddou is crossed by the footbridge.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Lunch is usually a set menu of salads, a tagine and fruit, or a Berber omelette cooked in a clay dish. Look for local almonds and walnuts sold by the roadside on the Tichka.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The hairpin bends below the Tichka pass.
• Ait Ben Haddou from across the river, in late morning or afternoon light.
• The view from the granary at the top of the ksar.
• The painted ceilings of Taourirt or Telouet.

ACCESSIBILITY
The climb inside Ait Ben Haddou is steep and uneven; if walking is difficult, you can enjoy the classic view of the ksar from the river bank and the new village. The Taourirt kasbah has several staircases.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: the High Atlas and the gateway to the Sahara in a single day.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: Ait Ben Haddou is about 190 km from Marrakech, around 4 hours each way with stops, or about 400 km in total. It is a long day, but the road over the Tichka is one of the most beautiful in Morocco and your driver stops whenever you like.

faq.question: Is a guide included?
faq.answer: Yes, a local guide leads the visit of Ait Ben Haddou. Your driver explains the road and the region, and can arrange a guide in Ouarzazate or Telouet if you would like one.

faq.question: Are entrance fees included?
faq.answer: No. Entering Ait Ben Haddou is free, though some houses ask a small fee to see inside. Tickets for the Taourirt kasbah, the film studios or the Telouet kasbah are paid on the spot in dirhams.

faq.question: Should we choose Ouarzazate or Telouet?
faq.answer: Ouarzazate is the classic choice, with the Taourirt kasbah and the film studios, and suits film fans and families. Telouet is quieter: a detour on the old caravan road to the Glaoui palace, with some of the finest tiles and painted ceilings in the south. You can choose when booking or on the day.

faq.question: Which films were made in Ait Ben Haddou?
faq.answer: The ksar and its surroundings have appeared in many films and series, including Lawrence of Arabia, The Mummy, Gladiator, Kingdom of Heaven and Game of Thrones. Your guide shows you where some of the scenes were shot.

faq.question: Can I stay overnight instead?
faq.answer: Yes. You can add a night in Ait Ben Haddou to enjoy the ksar at sunset and sunrise, when it is empty, or continue to the desert. Ask us and we will adapt the trip.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No, so you can choose where and what to eat. Your driver suggests restaurants with views of the ksar, usually with a set menu of salads, tagine and fruit.

faq.question: Is the trip suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, if they are fine with a long day in the car. Children usually love climbing through the ksar and the film studios. Bring snacks and entertainment, and tell us if you need child seats.

faq.question: Is the trip private?
faq.answer: Yes. The vehicle and driver are for your group only, so you choose the pick-up time, the stops and how long you stay at each place.

faq.question: When is the best time?
faq.answer: All year. Spring and autumn are the most comfortable. In summer Ait Ben Haddou is hot in the middle of the day, so we suggest an early start. In winter the pass may be snowy and the driver checks the road before leaving.

faq.question: Is the road safe? I get car sick.
faq.answer: The road is fully paved and well maintained, but it has many bends over the pass. If you get car sick, take medication before leaving, sit in front and ask your driver for extra stops and a gentle pace.

faq.question: What should I bring and wear?
faq.answer: A warm layer for the pass, a hat, sunglasses and sun cream for Ait Ben Haddou, shoes with a good grip for the steps of the ksar, and cash in dirhams for lunch, fees and small purchases. Light clothing that covers shoulders is respectful in the villages.

faq.question: Can we add a camel ride?
faq.answer: Short camel rides are sometimes offered near Ait Ben Haddou, but there are no dunes here. If a camel ride in the sand matters to you, the 2-day Zagora tour or the 3-day Merzouga tour are a much better choice.
